GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2014-03-20T15:02:01Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: potential bug in quoteIdentifiers function in query generator of mysql / mariadb
Description: hi,

i have an problem with multi associated properties in where and order conditions with nested eager loading.

i get wrong sql with the following find / findAll ...

``` javascript
var Article = sequelize.define('Article', { name: Sequelize.STRING })
  , Customer = sequelize.define('Customer', { name: Sequelize.STRING })
  , PostCode = sequelize.define('PostCode', { postcode: Sequelize.INTEGER, city: Sequelize.STRING })

Article.belongsTo(Customer)
Customer.belongsTo(PostCode)

sequelize.sync().done(function() {
  Article.findAll({
    attributes: ['name'],
    include: [{
      model: Customer,
      attributes: ['name'],
      include: [{
        model: PostCode,
        attributes: ['postcode', 'city'],
      }]
    }],
    order: ['Customer.PostCode.postcode', 'ASC']
  }).success(function(articles) {
    console.log('articles', articles)
  })
})
```

``` sql
SELECT
  `Article`.`name`,
  `Customer`.`name` AS `Customer.name`,
  `Customer`.`id` AS `Customer.id`,
  `Customer.PostCode`.`postcode` AS `Customer.PostCode.postcode`,
  `Customer.PostCode`.`city` AS `Customer.PostCode.city`,
  `Customer.PostCode`.`id` AS `Customer.PostCode.id`
FROM `Article`
  LEFT OUTER JOIN `Customer` AS `Customer`
    ON `Customer`.`id` = `Article`.`customer_id`
      LEFT OUTER JOIN `PostCode` AS `Customer.PostCode`
        ON `Customer.PostCode`.`id` = `Customer`.`post_code_id`
ORDER BY `Customer`.`PostCode`.`postcode`, `ASC`;
```

i think the problem is the quoteIdentifiers from lib/dialects/mysql/query-generator.js. it escapes the string 

```
Customer.PostCode.postcode
```

 to 

```
`Customer`.`PostCode`.`postcode`
```

To make the query working it should by 

```
`Customer.PostCode`.`postcode`
```

 cause of the generated table alias.

the problem could by solved by the following code ...

``` javascript
    quoteIdentifiers: function(identifiers, force) {
      var seperator = identifiers.lastIndexOf('.')
      if (seperator === -1) {
        return this.quoteIdentifier(identifiers, force)
      } else {
        return this.quoteIdentifier(identifiers.substr(0, seperator), force) + '.' + this.quoteIdentifier(identifiers.substr(seperator + 1), force)
      }   
    },
```

but i am not sure we're using that the right way. it would be nice if somebody can look over it.

thx, mithrandir
